questions.question: You want a permanent explanation on a cell, such as why a client gift was claimed, with no replies needed. What should you add?

answerOptions.text: A threaded comment with an @mention
answerOptions.rationale: Comments are for conversations that need replies.

answerOptions.text: A note (Review > Notes > New Note)
answerOptions.rationale: A note is a simple sticky label with no replies.

answerOptions.text: Data validation input message
answerOptions.rationale: That shows a prompt when a cell is selected, which is not meant for this.

answerOptions.text: A new column of text beside the data
answerOptions.rationale: That clutters the data instead of labelling one cell.

questions.question: In a shared file, you want to filter to the South region without hiding rows for colleagues who have it open. What should you use?

answerOptions.text: View > Sheet View > New, then filter
answerOptions.rationale: A Sheet View filters and sorts only for you.

answerOptions.text: Turn on the normal filter with Command Shift F
answerOptions.rationale: A normal filter in a shared file hides rows for everyone.

answerOptions.text: Switch on AutoSave before filtering
answerOptions.rationale: AutoSave saves changes; the filter still applies to everyone.

answerOptions.text: Hide the other regions' rows
answerOptions.rationale: Hidden rows are hidden for everyone too.

questions.question: On Excel for Mac, where do you find older saved versions of a file on OneDrive?

answerOptions.text: Review > Track Changes
answerOptions.rationale: Track Changes was removed and replaced by co-authoring.

answerOptions.text: Edit > Undo history
answerOptions.rationale: Undo only covers recent changes in the current session.

answerOptions.text: Data > Refresh All
answerOptions.rationale: Refresh All updates queries and pivots, not file versions.

answerOptions.text: File > Browse Version History, or click the file name in the title bar
answerOptions.rationale: Version history lists saved copies by date and author.

questions.question: You click Protect Sheet straight away, and now nobody can type in the input cells. What is the right order?

answerOptions.text: Protect Sheet first, then unlock the input cells
answerOptions.rationale: Locked status cannot be changed while the sheet is protected.

answerOptions.text: Tick Hidden on the input cells
answerOptions.rationale: Hidden only hides formulas from the formula bar.

answerOptions.text: Unlock the input cells in Format Cells > Protection, then Protect Sheet
answerOptions.rationale: Every cell is locked by default, so unlock inputs before protecting.

answerOptions.text: Use Protect Workbook instead of Protect Sheet
answerOptions.rationale: Workbook protection guards sheet structure, not cell entry.

questions.question: What stops users from deleting, renaming or adding sheets?

answerOptions.text: Review > Protect Workbook with Structure ticked
answerOptions.rationale: Structure protection locks the sheet list.

answerOptions.text: Review > Protect Sheet
answerOptions.rationale: Sheet protection guards cells, not the sheet itself.

answerOptions.text: Ticking Locked on every cell
answerOptions.rationale: Locked applies to cells and only works with sheet protection.

answerOptions.text: Saving the file as a template
answerOptions.rationale: A template protects the master file, not the sheets inside a copy.

questions.question: A 60-row sales register has nine columns and the last ones spill onto extra pages. Which scaling setting suits it best?

answerOptions.text: Fit Sheet on One Page
answerOptions.rationale: Sixty rows squeezed onto one sheet become too small to read.

answerOptions.text: Set the scaling to 100%
answerOptions.rationale: That leaves the last columns spilling onto extra pages.

answerOptions.text: Portrait with no print area
answerOptions.rationale: Portrait makes the width problem worse.

answerOptions.text: Fit to 1 page wide, with the tall box left blank
answerOptions.rationale: All columns fit across, and the rows use as many pages as needed.

questions.question: A2 holds a linked Stocks value. You type =A2.Capital and get #FIELD!. Why?

answerOptions.text: You are not connected to the internet
answerOptions.rationale: Being offline stops refresh, but #FIELD! points to a wrong field.

answerOptions.text: Field names must always be in square brackets
answerOptions.rationale: Brackets are only needed for names with spaces or symbols.

answerOptions.text: A Stocks record has no Capital field; only use fields that exist for that data type
answerOptions.rationale: #FIELD! means the field does not exist for that type.

answerOptions.text: Stock prices are delayed by some minutes
answerOptions.rationale: A delay affects the price, not whether a field exists.

questions.question: The Accessibility Checker warns about merged cells in the invoice title A1:F1. How do you keep it centred without merging?

answerOptions.text: Add alt text to the title
answerOptions.rationale: Alt text is for pictures, charts and shapes.

answerOptions.text: Unmerge, then Format Cells > Alignment > Horizontal: Center Across Selection
answerOptions.rationale: It looks the same and avoids merged cells.

answerOptions.text: Change the font colour to Automatic
answerOptions.rationale: That fixes contrast, not merged cells.

answerOptions.text: Merge the cells again with Merge Across
answerOptions.rationale: That is still a merge, so the warning stays.
